facts.text: Only two major-college teams of the 1980s averaged 100 points a game (15+ games): Loyola Marymount (3×, best 1989-90: 122.4 ppg, 26-6); Oklahoma (3×, best 1987-88: 102.9 ppg, 35-4).
Only two major-college players of the 1980s made 100 threes as a freshman: Alphonso Ford (1989-90: 104 threes); Tony Ross (1986-87: 104 threes).
Only two major-college players of the 1980s recorded 80 steals and 80 blocks: Carey Scurry (1983-84: 92 stl, 115 blk); Harold Pressley (1985-86: 83 stl, 83 blk).

Just three major-college players of the 1980s scored 1000 points: Bo Kimble (1989-90: 1,131 pts in 32 games); Hersey Hawkins Jr (1987-88: 1,125 pts in 31 games); Hank Gathers (1988-89: 1,015 pts in 31 games).

Just four major-college players of the 1980s blocked 160 shots: David Robinson (1985-86: 207 blocks); Hakeem Olajuwon (2×, best 1983-84: 207 blocks); Alonzo Mourning (1988-89: 169 blocks); Benoit Benjamin (1984-85: 162 blocks).

Just three major-college players of the 1980s scored 800 points without making a three: Hank Gathers (1988-89: 1,015 pts, 0 threes); Armen Gilliam (1986-87: 903 pts, 0 threes); Stacey King (2×, best 1987-88: 869 pts, 0 threes).

Just three major-college players of the 1980s recorded 100 blocks and 100 assists: Derrick Coleman (1988-89: 127 blk, 106 ast); Luc Longley (1989-90: 117 blk, 108 ast); Pervis Ellison (1987-88: 102 blk, 108 ast).
Only two major-college players of the 1980s averaged 25 points a game as a freshman (15+ games): Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf (1988-89: 30.2 ppg); Alphonso Ford (1989-90: 29.9 ppg).
Just three major-college teams of the 1980s lost 27 games: George Washington (1988-89: 1-27); U.S. Int'l (1984-85: 1-27); Pacific (1983-84: 3-27).
Most 25-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 1980s: Alfredrick Hughes, 3 (1982-83, 1983-84, 1984-85).
Most 800-point seasons in the 1980s: Wayman Tisdale, 3 (1982-83, 1983-84, 1984-85).

Just four major-college players of the 1980s averaged 14 rebounds a game (15+ games): Xavier McDaniel (2×, best 1984-85: 14.8 rpg); Benoit Benjamin (1984-85: 14.1 rpg); Carey Scurry (1984-85: 14.1 rpg); Darryl Watson (1980-81: 14.0 rpg).

Just three major-college players of the 1980s averaged 12 rebounds a game as a freshman (15+ games): Kenny Miller (1987-88: 13.6 rpg); Michael Cage (1980-81: 13.1 rpg); Shaquille O'Neal (1989-90: 12.0 rpg).

Just four major-college players of the 1980s averaged 10 assists a game (15+ games): Avery Johnson (2×, best 1987-88: 13.3 apg); Anthony Manuel (1987-88: 12.0 apg); Leon Wood III (1982-83: 11.0 apg); Mark Wade (1986-87: 10.7 apg).
9 major-college players dished out 300 assists in the 1980s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Mark Wade, 1986-87 — 406 assists.
6 major-college players recorded 130 steals in the 1980s (7 seasons). The most extreme: Mookie Blaylock, 1987-88 — 150 steals.
6 major-college players made 130 threes in the 1980s. The most extreme: Darrin Fitzgerald, 1986-87 — 158 threes.
Highest scoring average in a season in the 1980s: Hersey Hawkins Jr, Bradley, 1987-88 — 36.3 ppg.
Most 800-point seasons by one school's players in the 1980s: Oklahoma, 6 (Wayman Tisdale, Stacey King, Harvey Grant).
Most points in a season in the 1980s: Bo Kimble, Loyola Marymount, 1989-90 — 1,131.
Most 12-rebound-per-game seasons (15+ games) by one school's players in the 1980s: Loyola Chicago, 4 (Kenny Miller, Wayne Sappleton, Andre Moore).
Highest rebounding average in a season in the 1980s: Xavier McDaniel, Wichita State, 1984-85 — 14.8 rpg.
Most 200-free-throw seasons by one school's players in the 1980s: Missouri, 3 (Derrick Chievous, Byron Irvin).
Most free throws made in a season in the 1980s: Hersey Hawkins Jr, Bradley, 1987-88 — 284.
Best field-goal percentage in a season (200+ attempts) in the 1980s: Steve Johnson, Oregon State, 1980-81 — 0.746%.
Best free-throw percentage in a season (100+ attempts) in the 1980s: Rod Foster, UCLA, 1981-82 — 0.95%.
Highest assist average in a season in the 1980s: Avery Johnson, Southern, 1987-88 — 13.3 apg.
Most 3-block-per-game seasons (15+ games) by one school's players in the 1980s: Georgetown, 6 (Alonzo Mourning, Dikembe Mutombo, Patrick Ewing).
Highest blocks average in a season in the 1980s: David Robinson, Navy, 1985-86 — 5.9 bpg.
Highest steals average in a season in the 1980s: Darron Brittman, Chicago State, 1985-86 — 5.0 spg.
Most threes in a season in the 1980s: Darrin Fitzgerald, Butler, 1986-87 — 158.
Highest team scoring average in a season in the 1980s: Loyola Marymount, 1989-90 — 122.4 ppg (26-6).
Best team field-goal percentage in a season in the 1980s: Michigan, 1988-89 — 0.566%.
Most team threes in a season in the 1980s: UNLV, 1986-87 — 309.
Most 100-three seasons by one school's players in the 1980s: Mississippi Valley State, 4 (Tim Pollard, George Ivory, Alphonso Ford).
Most points of the 1980s: Lionel Simmons, 3,217.
Most rebounds of the 1980s: Derrick Coleman, 1,537.
Most free throws made in the 1980s: Derrick Chievous, 764.
Most assists of the 1980s: Sherman Douglas, 960.
Most threes of the 1980s: Jeff Fryer, 363.
Most blocks of the 1980s: David Robinson, 516.
Most steals of the 1980s: Chipper Harris, 450.
6 major-college teams won 35 games in the 1980s (7 seasons). The most extreme: UNLV, 1986-87 — 37-2.
8 major-college players averaged 30 points a game (15+ games) in the 1980s. The most extreme: Hersey Hawkins Jr, 1987-88 — 36.3 ppg.
12 major-college players averaged 20 points and 12 rebounds (15+ games) in the 1980s (14 seasons). The most extreme: Hank Gathers, 1988-89 — 32.7 ppg, 13.7 rpg.
5 major-college players averaged 5 blocks a game (15+ games) in the 1980s (7 seasons). The most extreme: David Robinson, 1985-86 — 5.9 bpg.
10 major-college players averaged 4 steals a game (15+ games) in the 1980s (13 seasons). The most extreme: Darron Brittman, 1985-86 — 5.0 spg.

method: College basketball (men's): each line is one Stathead (Sports Reference college basketball) Season Finder query over the decade's ten seasons (a decade is the seasons starting in its years: the 1970s run 1970-71 to 1979-80), run in a signed-in subscriber session; result rows and stable ids are stored as provenance.

Sports Reference's season finders begin with 1947-48, so the 1940s page covers two seasons and earlier decades are not in the record. Rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and the three-pointer (1986-87) arrive at different times; rules on a stat a season lacks return nothing. Per-game figures are totals divided by games.
